Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

"You probably mean org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarConstants.CHKSUM_OFFSET. It looks like:
```java
81 :     int    CHKSUM_OFFSET = 148;
```"

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test org.apache.commons.compress.DetectArchiverTestCase.testCOMPRESS335 invokes processing of the "COMPRESS-335.tar" archive, which has a checksum in its header that is right aligned with zero padding on the left instead of the expected NULL-SPACE terminator on the right. The checksum verification is performed by the method org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[]).

Inspecting verifyCheckSum reveals the method reads up to 6 octal digit characters ('0' to '7') starting from the checksum offset (148) with length 8 bytes in the tar header. During this, it accumulates the stored checksum value by parsing these digits. If a non-digit or a terminating character is encountered, it stops processing the digits and replaces the checksum field bytes with spaces for the sum calculation.

The code expects digits in the first 6 positions within the checksum field, and if digits appear only right aligned with zero padding on the left (likely in later positions), these digits can be skipped or ignored because digits past the 6th position are not processed due to the digits < 6 condition in the loop. Consequently, the last two checksum digits are lost, rendering the comparison to the computed sum invalid and causing the checksum verification to fail.

This explains the failing test: The archive "COMPRESS-335.tar" contains a checksum that has zero padding on the left rather than the expected trailing space or null terminator right aligned, causing the stored checksum digits not to be fully parsed. The sum checking logic inadequately handles this format assumption.

The core of the issue is the condition `digits++ < 6` which caps the digits selectively, not accommodating checksums that might appear right aligned with zero padding on the left instead of the conventional left aligned with trailing space.

Recent bug reports related to TAR archives focus on size and directory entry issues but do not describe checksum format differences or parsing bugs, so they are not directly relevant here.

Hence, to fix the test failure, the checksum verification logic in org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[]) should be adjusted to correctly accommodate trailing spaces and left zero padding checksum formats, probably by reconsidering the strict digit count limit and the padding characters accepted.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
